title: Korean Ship With 3,000 Cars Arrives at Mexico’s Interoceanic Corridor
author: Hiram Moreno
content:
_This article by Hiram Moreno originally appeared in the[July 10, 2026 edition
of La Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/2026/07/10/estados/025n1est),
Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Salina Cruz, Oax.** As part of the Interoceanic Corridor of the Isthmus of
Tehuantepec (CIIT) project, promoted during the government of Andrés Manuel
López Obrador, **last night the ship Glovis Condor arrived at the dock of the
National Port System Administration (Asipona) in Salina Cruz, having set sail
from the port of Masan, in South Korea, with 3,000 Hyundai vehicles that will
be transported along the CIIT lines to Coatzacoalcos, Veracruz, to be shipped
again toward the east coast of the United States.**

The transport of the vehicles will be carried out using Bi-Max and Tri-Max
type railcars of the Isthmus of Tehuantepec Railway (FIT), which arrived in
Salina Cruz yesterday morning for the interoceanic crossing from the Pacific
to the Gulf of Mexico, and then to send them to the U.S. market.

This will be the second crossing of Hyundai cars through the CIIT; the first
was in March 2025, when, as part of the CIIT pilot tests, 900 units were
transported along the same route. Now there are 3,000 new vehicles that set
sail from South Korea this past June 22, and they will be in Coatzacoalcos on
July 12 for a journey that will last 20 days.

According to local authorities, Hyundai's confidence consolidates the CIIT as
an important means for transporting goods between destinations around the
world, and in particular Asia and the Americas.

The idea of establishing an industrial development in the Isthmus through
which intermediate and final goods would be produced had been pending for
several six-year terms, with the so-called special economic zones that would
be granted as concessions to private investors.

The project promoted by López Obrador set the goal of modernizing the Isthmus
of Tehuantepec Railway as the backbone for moving goods between the ports of
Salina Cruz and Coatzacoalcos.
